title: Planarity of Organic Molecules
page_title: Planarity of Organic Molecules | Cambridge (CIE) AS Chemistry Revision Notes 2023

titles.section: 13. An Introduction to AS Level Organic Chemistry
titles.topic: Shapes of Organic Molecules; σ & π Bonds

blocks.md:
- Planar molecules have all their atoms in the same plane

  - E.g. linear, bent, trigonal planar and square planar

blocks.alt: Diagram of molecular shapes: linear, non-linear (bent), trigonal planar, and square planar, showing bond angles of 180°, 104.5°, 120°, and 90°.
blocks.caption: The diagram shows molecules which have all their atoms in the same plane with their name and the associated bond angle

blocks.md:
- The presence of an sp<sup>2</sup> hybridised carbon can force the molecule to adopt a planar configuration **(trigonal planar**)
- The 3 σ bonds position themselves in a trigonal planar position so that the bonding pair of electrons are as far away from each other and therefore minimise the repulsion between them

blocks.alt: Diagram of ethene showing structural formula and ball-and-stick model, illustrating trigonal planar geometry of carbon atoms and hydrogen bonds.
blocks.caption: Ethene is a planar molecule with two trigonal planar centres around the carbon atoms

blocks.alt: Structural diagrams of propene, showing molecular geometry: tetrahedral and trigonal planar centres, with hydrogen and carbon atoms labelled.
blocks.caption: Propene has two trigonal planar centres around the carbon-carbon double bond and one tetrahedral centre

blocks.md:
- The presence of an sp hybridised carbon can also force the molecule to adopt a planar configuration (**linear**)
- The 2 σ bonds position themselves in a linear position to minimise the repulsion between the bonding pairs of electrons

blocks.alt: Diagram of ethyne molecule, showing its linear structure. Includes chemical formula HC≡CH, with hydrogen and carbon atoms in blue and pink circles.
blocks.caption: Ethyne is a planar molecule with one planar centre: the molecule is linear

blocks.alt: Propyne, HC≡CCH3, shown as a structural formula and a ball-and-stick model: the three carbons and the first hydrogen lie on a straight line, and the CH3 group is a tetrahedral centre
blocks.caption: Propyne has one planar centre around the carbon-carbon triple bond (linear) and one tetrahedral centre
